source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-09-13. Based on the GOLD 2023 and 2024 reports. Not tied to an article; review before trusting.

questions.q: What post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio confirms airflow obstruction in COPD?
questions.why: The fixed ratio over-diagnoses in the elderly and under-diagnoses in the young, but it is what the guideline uses. Severity is then graded by FEV1 percent predicted.

questions.q: GOLD grade 3, severe, corresponds to what FEV1 range?
questions.why: Grade 1 is 80% or more, grade 2 is 50% to 79%, grade 4 is under 30%. The grade describes obstruction; the letter group describes symptoms and exacerbations, and drives treatment.

questions.q: What places a patient in GOLD group E?
questions.a: Two or more moderate exacerbations, or one needing admission, in the past year
d: A CAT score of 10 or more
questions.why: Groups A and B are separated by symptoms alone. Group E replaced the old C and D because exacerbation history, not symptom burden, is what changes the first prescription.

questions.q: What is the recommended initial inhaler therapy for group B?
questions.why: Dual long-acting bronchodilation is now the starting point for both B and E. Group A gets a single bronchodilator, short or long acting.

questions.q: At what blood eosinophil count does adding an inhaled corticosteroid to LABA-LAMA become favoured in a patient who exacerbates?
questions.why: Between 100 and 300 it is considered. Under 100, or with repeated pneumonia or mycobacterial infection, the corticosteroid is avoided.

questions.q: During a COPD exacerbation, which findings justify an antibiotic?
a: Increased sputum purulence with increased volume or dyspnoea
questions.why: Purulence is the best bedside marker of bacterial infection. Five to seven days of amoxicillin-clavulanate, a macrolide or doxycycline is typical.

questions.q: What oral prednisone course is standard for a COPD exacerbation?
d: 60 mg daily for 10 days with a taper
options: 60 mg daily for 10 days with a taper
questions.why: Five days was as good as fourteen in the REDUCE trial with fewer steroid effects. No taper is needed.

questions.q: What oxygen saturation is targeted during a COPD exacerbation?
questions.why: Higher targets raise the carbon dioxide in patients who retain it. A blood gas 30 to 60 minutes after starting oxygen checks for that.

questions.q: At rest and clinically stable, at or below what PaO2 does long-term oxygen improve survival?
questions.why: Or a saturation of 88% or less. The threshold rises to 59 mm Hg with cor pulmonale or polycythaemia. Oxygen for exertional desaturation alone does not improve survival.

questions.q: Which single intervention most slows the decline in lung function in COPD?
questions.why: Pulmonary rehabilitation is the intervention that most reduces admissions after an exacerbation, and is recommended for anyone in group B or E.

questions.q: A former smoker keeps exacerbating on LABA-LAMA-ICS. Which add-on is an option?
questions.why: Roflumilast is the other option, for FEV1 under 50% with chronic bronchitis. Azithromycin is reserved for former smokers because it did not help current smokers, and hearing and QT are monitored.

questions.q: Which vaccines are recommended for adults with COPD?
questions.why: Tdap and zoster follow the general adult schedule. Influenza vaccination reduces both exacerbations and deaths in this group.
